summary: The service started this run, not an instruction: the width-200 nudge loop at f* 0.74 (job 164676, E0075) had ended. There were no Asked items, so nothing went unanswered, and no time went to unasked work. No claims were proposed or changed, and no claims or blockers are open on this line. All three of my points from the last review were answered, correctly. (1) The false sentence that every width-100 nudge loop stopped at Gamma 4.4 is corrected in the summary, PROGRAM.md and progress.md (five of eight stopped at 4.45, two at 4.4 and one at 4.5). (2) The up cap of the nudge loops is now given as sixteen times width 100's, not four times. (3) The 09:50Z stamps in the two E0076 evidence files are now 09:37Z, with a note of the correction. The collected numbers reproduce exactly. I compared all sixty per-step entries for this loop in evidence/E0076-interim.json with the sixty mirrored summary.json files. SHA-256, Gamma, outcome, cycles, CPU-hours, energy gains, audit failures and slow stretches all match, with zero mismatches. Fifty-eight steps completed, and the steps sum to 76.63 CPU-hours, against 77.1 in the job record. The floor stop is the two CPU-hour cap at Gamma 2.25 after twenty-three of twenty-five cycles. The top stop is the eight CPU-hour cap at 4.5 after twelve cycles. There was no stall, energy gain, audit failure or slow stretch, so the referee check on slow stretches before a stop is clean. The cost per cycle at width 200 reproduces: 188.6 CPU-seconds at Gamma 4.35, 284.8 at 4.4, 690.6 at 4.45 and 2404.9 at 4.5. The width-100 loop (E0065) reproduces too: floor 2.05, with a half-hour cap stop at 2.0 after twenty cycles, and top 4.4, with a half-hour cap stop at 4.45 after sixteen cycles. I recomputed the matched-step cost ratios from E0065 and the mirror and got the same medians: 8.8 going down (fourteen pairs) and 7.7 going up (forty-two pairs). The reading that all four ends are cost stops and say nothing about box size is right. So is the reading that width 200's extra step at 4.45 reflects its budget. Width 100's cost at 4.45 (112.9 CPU-seconds per cycle) means twenty-five cycles would take about 0.78 CPU-hours. That is well inside any cap matched to width 200's eight hours. One sentence is wrong. The second proposed direction's rationale says 'Every nudge and baseline floor so far is a cost floor at both widths. The up caps (sixteen times) already exceed the measured cost ratio, so they need no change.' Both halves hold only for the nudge loops (E0075). They do not hold for the baseline loops (E0076). In evidence/E0076-results.json the baseline floor at f* 0.65 is a physical stop at both widths and is listed among the comparable ends. At the f* 0.38 baseline floor, width 100 stopped on a sphere overlap. The baseline up caps were 2.0 against 8.0 CPU-hours, so four times, not sixteen (D0046 and every E0076 job record), while the measured baseline up-step cost ratios are 7.4 to 11.4. The same nudge-only figure appears unqualified in lines/L0018/progress.md ('up caps (16 times) already exceed it'). The fix is to say 'nudge' in both places and to add that the baseline up caps were four times, below the cost ratio. Two smaller points. First, the line state's closes_when still says the cost ratio is 'about seven times on the way down'; the nudge loops now measure 7.6 and 8.8, so that number is stale. Second, the comparison at the top used only E0065, with its half-hour up cap. The E0072 continuations of those width-100 nudge loops, with a two CPU-hour up cap, got one step further at every f* (sessions/2026-11-20-L0015.json). That is a closer budget match for width 200's eight hours, and it would likely show width 100 also completing 4.45 at f* 0.74. Neither point changes a conclusion. The line state for this line ('Wider or deeper box', L0018) otherwise says what the evidence says. Its new f* 0.74 sentence and the narrowed 'for this f*' wording of the f* 0.38 wall are right. program check passes. The latest approval is still approved/20261124T031934297997Z (Nov 24 03:19), so none were made in the last day. It counts 561.4 of 10000 weekly CPU-hours. My earlier count of about 877 plus this job's 77.1 gives about 954, as the run says, so program check still undercounts ended jobs. sequel-data is 684 megabytes against a 15 gigabyte ceiling. Free disk is 90 gigabytes against a 40 gigabyte floor. sequel-data/tmp/ is empty, and active.jsonl is empty. Outside the two allowed folders, the only writes since the run began are the harness's own folders and the uv cache. As the user instructed, this review is committed on branch line/L0018 in the line's worktree, not on main.

run_conditions.assessment: This was a four-minute service run, from 11:25:38 to 11:29:41 by its own record. Its main commit landed at 11:29:41, and a second commit at 11:29:59 corrected the recorded end from 11:31:00 to the measured 11:29:41. It started about a minute after the service recorded the ended job at 11:24:25. It collected the one ended loop, compared it with the width-100 nudge loop, and answered all three of my points. It started nothing, cancelled nothing and left no local jobs. Seventeen width-200 loops are still on Hatteras: ten without friction (E0074) and seven with the nudge (E0075). The host is a Linux container, so pmset is unavailable and sleep could not be measured, as the summary says. Local CPU of 0.01 hours fits a run of reading and writing. Free disk of 90 gigabytes matches what I see. The cores_available figure of 23.7 is the forty cores minus the load average, as the summary explains. The load average is now 2.1, so that figure was a snapshot. The machine did not limit the science. The loop's own step caps set both ends at both widths, and the summary says this is a limit of the design. The job's 77.1 CPU-hours are under the 100 CPU-hour per-run limit.
discrepancies: scheduled_start is the service's job-record commit (11:24:25Z), not a measured runner start, as the summary itself says.
